title: Initiative by Else Went at The Public Theater #initiativeplay #thepub...
transcript: Come with me to a 5-hour play — on a weeknight, no less. Initiative by Else Went follows a group of high schoolers in the early 2000s over the course of four years. It's a vast and episodic piece that's ambitious both to its credit and to a fault. Generally though, I was impressed by all the performances, the writing, and the direction. It feels of its time, with nods to IM culture and some of the political happenings, but doesn't feel dated at all. I think it does a great job capturing the undeniable ache of adolescence — the feeling of having the weight of the world on your shoulders, the sense of personal insecurity, the stock you put into how others perceive you, and how important relationships and community become when it feels like that's all you have. These themes are most well-rendered in the intimate, two-hander scenes, though I wish there had been some more ensemble work — this could have kept things moving a bit more as well. Now, did the play have to be over five hours long to capture these themes? Probably not. I ultimately found its run time to be a bit arduous and slightly detrimental to my overall experience. That said, I was pretty invested in every character by the end, despite not initially being captured by any of them. I can't say this would have happened in two or three hours, and character growth is a major component of the story here. So if you think you can handle it, it's a satisfying journey. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
